name: Ohio
standard: WCAG 2.1 AA (Ohio Administrative Policy IT-09 Digital Accessibility, aligned to ADA Title II rule)

laws.cite: 28 CFR Part 35, Subpart H (ADA Title II web/mobile rule, 2024; compliance dates extended by DOJ IFR effective 2026-04-20)
laws.summary: Requires state and local government web content and mobile apps to conform to WCAG 2.1 AA, with compliance dates now 2027-04-26 (population 50,000+) and 2028-04-26 (smaller entities and special districts).

policy_docs.title: Ohio Administrative Policy IT-09 Digital Accessibility (DAS; reported updated January 2025)
Ohio Administrative Policy IT-08 Website Standardization

applies_to: State agencies, boards and commissions under the authority of the Governor; public-facing web content, web apps and mobile apps, including contracted/third-party solutions. Local governments not covered by IT-09 (ADA Title II floor applies).

deadlines.what: IT-09: agency web content and mobile applications must conform to WCAG 2.1 AA.
ADA Title II floor: local entities under 50,000 population and special district governments (extended from 2027-04-26).

requires: Agency Digital Accessibility strategy for public-facing web content and mobile apps
Accessibility statement on each agency homepage and app with feedback options and contact info from the ADA Coordinators Directory
Use DAS InnovateOhio Platform design/content standards per IT-08
Contracts for third-party web content and mobile apps must require WCAG 2.1 AA
mobile: explicit — IT-09 covers agency mobile applications by name.
procurement: Agencies must require contracted, in-kind and third-party web content or mobile app solutions to meet the ADA Title II rule and WCAG 2.1 AA.
enforcement: Administrative policy enforced through DAS; public reports to accessibility@das.ohio.gov; ADA Title II complaints to DOJ.
notes: Every das.ohio.gov and ohio.gov page returned HTTP 404 to the fetcher, so IT-09 text was not opened. Details come from repeated search-result extracts of das.ohio.gov and agency accessibility pages; verify against the policy text before relying on it. No Ohio Revised Code section setting a web standard was found.
